parsed.why: State enforces against gender presentation: trans women jailed five years (statutory maximum) for women's clothing; police beat detainees, extort, prisons described as 'hell'; no recourse, venue raided. Near-certain severe punishment if outed.

Permissive law, marriage equality, anti-discrimination and hate-crime recourse, official trans-custody framework. Deductions: dating-app ambush network, rising far right, unresolved trans-specific hate-crime magnitude. Functioning institutions leave records.

No explicit statute, but police collectively detain lesbians, sexual violence against trans women in custody, conversion practices and forced impregnation, impunity for police/military perpetrators, pending criminalising draft. State practice, not paper, governs.

Strong self-ID, equal-treatment and marriage framework, but documented tier-1 exposures: trans prisoner moved to men's prison despite female marker, sauna guideline excluding trans women, unresolved airport screening complaint. Institutions enforce the hostile practice.

No criminalisation and unenforced ambiguous provision, but police use it as extortion pretext, no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse, 73% capital hostility, documented harassment. No trans-specific facility/custody exposure documented.
